paragraphs.zh: Tabelle 5:    Erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen der allgemeinen Formel (I), worin die Substituenten und Symbole folgende Bedeutungen haben:
paragraphs.en: Table 5:    Compounds according to the invention of the general formula (I), in which the substituents and symbols have the following meanings:
paragraphs.notes: The only German prose on the page. Printed over two lines with 'Tabelle 5:' in bold and the rest in the regular face; the second line is indented to align under 'Erfindungsgemäße'. Umlaut and eszett are as printed (Erfindungsgemäße). The caption states plainly that the table enumerates compounds of the invention, not prior art. The zh field carries the verbatim German, since this patent is German and not Chinese despite the field name.

paragraphs.zh: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Et R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.en: R2 = Cl R3 = SO2Et R4 = H R5 = H R6 = OH Y = CH2 Z = CH2 v = 1 w = 0
paragraphs.notes: The block of fixed substituent values printed under the caption, laid out as three rows of three definitions across the page. The superscript locants on R2 to R6 are printed as true superscripts and the digits of SO2Et and CH2 as true subscripts; both are flattened to plain text here, and the wide column gaps are approximated with spaces. These cells are chemical symbols and single letters, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string. An ink blot sits between the '=' and the 'H' of 'R4 = H', touching the left stem of the H; at 8x magnification it is a scan artifact and not a character, so it is not transcribed, but it is listed in illegible. R1 and R7a/R7b are NOT fixed here: they are the columns the table below varies.

paragraphs.notes: Markush enumeration table, compound numbers 517 to 530, with a shaded header row. The cells are chemical symbols and NMR data, not German prose, so zh and en are the same string; the only German in the grid is the header cell 'Physikalische Daten' ('Physical data'), left as printed. Typography as printed: the header cells R1, R7a and R7b carry superscripts; the digits in OCH2CF3, OCH2CF2H, OCH2CH2F, OCH2CH2Cl, OCH2CH2Br, O(CH2)2, CDCl3 and so on are subscripts, and the leading '1' of '1H NMR' is a superscript; all are rendered inline here. The chemical shift symbol at the head of the data cell is a lower case Greek delta, written 'd' here to keep the transcription ASCII, followed by a wide gap before the first shift, which is preserved. Only row 517 carries physical data; rows 518 to 530 have an empty Physikalische Daten cell as printed, recorded by the trailing ' | ' with nothing after it. Transcribed as printed without correction: row 517 reads '7.28 (d,1H), d,1H), 8.15 (d,1H)', so the second signal has a multiplicity and an integral but no chemical shift and no opening bracket; rows 518 and 523 print the identical R1 value OCH2CF3 with the identical Me, Me pair, so the two compound numbers differ in nothing that the table records. Row 524 carries a drawn ring in the R1 cell instead of text; a bracketed pointer stands in its place here and the structure itself is in drawings.

structures.position_in_drawing: 1st, centred between the fixed substituent block and the table header row; the generic scaffold that Tabelle 5 enumerates
structures.core: two rings joined by a ketone bridge: a cyclohex-2-ene-1,3-dione drawn in its enol form (3-hydroxycyclohex-2-en-1-one) on the left, and a benzene ring drawn with three inner double bonds on the right
substituents: on the cyclohexenone ring: OH at C3, drawn as a label above the top ring vertex, which carries the ring double bond
on the cyclohexenone ring: =O at C1, drawn as a doubly bonded O to the lower right of the ring
on the cyclohexenone ring: the aroyl bridge at C2, the vertex between the OH-bearing C3 and the =O-bearing C1, with the drawn double bond running C2=C3

on the cyclohexenone ring: R7a and R7b both at C6, the bottom vertex, which is adjacent to the C1 ketone carbon; each is drawn as its own bond down to a label, R7a to the lower left and R7b to the lower right
on the cyclohexenone ring: two unlabelled CH2 vertices at C4 and C5, on the left edge
bridge: C=O, drawn as a vertex with a doubly bonded O above it, joining C2 of the cyclohexenone to C1 of the benzene ring
on the benzene ring: the C=O bridge at C1 (the upper left vertex)
on the benzene ring: Cl at C2 (the top vertex)

on the benzene ring: CH2-R1 at C3, drawn as a bond from the ring up-right to an unlabelled apex vertex and a further bond from that apex down-right to the label R with superscript 1, so the linker is a single unlabelled CH2
on the benzene ring: SO2Me at C4, drawn as a bond from the ring down-right to the label SO2Me
on the benzene ring: H at C5 (a plain unlabelled ring vertex)
on the benzene ring: H at C6 (a plain unlabelled ring vertex)

drawings.notes: The locants above are a reading convention for this record and are not printed on the drawing. On the benzene ring C1 is the carbon bearing the ketone bridge and the numbering runs towards the chlorine, which sits on the adjacent carbon as drawn; the bridge, Cl, CH2-R1 and SO2Me occupy four consecutive ring carbons in that order and the two remaining vertices, on the lower left edge, are unlabelled. On the cyclohexenone ring C1 is the ketone carbon and C3 the enol carbon bearing OH, with the aroyl bridge on C2 between them; the gem pair R7a/R7b sits on C6, the vertex bonded directly to the C1 ketone carbon, with two unlabelled CH2 vertices between C6 and C3 on the far side of the ring. Every position is read off the drawing only; the scan is clean and no position is ambiguous. name and smiles are null because R1, R7a and R7b are undefined variables on this drawing: writing either would mean choosing values the drawing does not fix. presented_as is intermediate_structure in the sense this run uses for a generic Markush scaffold that a table enumerates; the caption above it says plainly that these are erfindungsgemäße Verbindungen (compounds according to the invention) of the general formula (I), so this is the invention's own subject matter and NOT prior art. There is no reaction scheme on this page and no arrow of any kind.

structures.position_in_drawing: 2nd, inside the R1 cell of the table, in the row numbered 524; it replaces the text that every other row prints in that column
structures.core: tetrahydrofuran (oxolane), a saturated five-membered ring with one ring oxygen, drawn with the O at the bottom vertex
substituents: at the ring carbon two bonds away from the ring O in one direction and one CH2 away in the other, that is the 3-position: a CH2 drawn as a bond up-left to an apex vertex
on that CH2: a horizontal bond left to a labelled O, which is the open valence of the fragment and is where it joins the rest of the molecule
structures.name: (tetrahydrofuran-3-yl)methoxy

drawings.notes: This is the R1 value for compound Nr. 524 of Tabelle 5, drawn rather than written. Ring connectivity read off the drawing: from the attachment carbon a bond runs right to a second carbon, down-right to a third, down-left to the ring O, and up-left to a fourth carbon that closes back to the attachment carbon, so the attachment carbon has one CH2 between it and the ring O on one side and two CH2 on the other, which fixes it as the 3-position. No wedge, hash or other stereo mark is drawn at that carbon, so the drawing does not fix the configuration and none is recorded. smiles is null because the fragment as drawn has an open valence on the leading O, where it attaches to the benzylic CH2 of the scaffold; a closed SMILES would have to add an atom the drawing does not show.

discrepancies.what: The drawn scaffold carries a methylsulfonyl group where the fixed substituent block above it defines an ethylsulfonyl group.
discrepancies.drawing_says: SO2Me, drawn as a bond from the benzene ring at the position para to the ketone bridge and ortho to the CH2-R1 arm, labelled SO2Me.
discrepancies.text_says: R3  =  SO2Et in the fixed substituent block printed directly above the drawing.

discrepancies.what: The only physical data on the page, the 1H NMR of Nr. 517, contains a three proton singlet and no ethyl pattern in the region where the fixed substituent block's SO2Et would put a triplet and a quartet.
discrepancies.drawing_says: SO2Me on the benzene ring, a group that accounts for a single three proton singlet.
discrepancies.text_says: R3  =  SO2Et in the fixed substituent block, and the row 517 data cell '3.3 (s,3H)' with no triplet near 1.3 and no quartet near 3.9 anywhere in the list.

discrepancies.what: The fixed substituent block defines nine symbols, but only R2, R3 and R6 can be matched to a label or a drawn group on the scaffold; R4, R5, Y, Z, v and w appear nowhere on the drawing.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The benzene ring carries Cl and SO2Me as drawn text, the cyclohexenone carries a drawn OH, the linker to R1 is an unlabelled CH2 apex, and the remaining ring vertices are plain unlabelled vertices with no R4, R5, Y, Z, v or w label anywhere on the page.
discrepancies.text_says: R2 = Cl, R3 = SO2Et, R4 = H, R5 = H, R6 = OH, Y = CH2, Z = CH2, v = 1, w = 0.

discrepancies.what: Compound numbers 518 and 523 are printed with identical values in every column the table records.
discrepancies.drawing_says: The scaffold is the same single drawing for every row, so nothing outside the R1 and R7a/R7b columns can distinguish the two rows.
discrepancies.text_says: Row 518: 'OCH2CF3 | Me, Me'. Row 523: 'OCH2CF3 | Me, Me'.

illegible: An ink blot roughly one character wide sits between the '=' and the 'H' of 'R4  =  H' in the third column of the fixed substituent block, touching the left stem of the H. At 8x magnification it has no letter shape and is read as a scan artifact rather than a character, so the definition is transcribed as 'R4  =  H'; if it is in fact printed matter, what it says is unreadable.
A single stray dot sits in the wide blank area below the table, roughly centred on the page. It carries no text and is read as a scan speck.
